fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When a few mothers lay eggs on a patch and their offspring mate there before the daughters disperse, the evolutionarily stable sex ratio is female-biased, and the bias weakens as the number of mothers grows.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: unbeatable proportion of males x^* = \frac{n-1}{2n} for n foundresses per patch (diploid case)

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: W. D. Hamilton (1967) Extraordinary Sex Ratios

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: n foundresses per patch, mating confined to the natal patch, only females disperse, mothers control the sex ratio

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: proved as an ESS within the model. Haplodiploidy and inbreeding shift x* slightly.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: unbeatable proportion of males x^* = \frac{n-1}{2n} for n foundresses per patch (diploid case)

fields.label: Proposed test
fields.value: Vary the number of foundresses per host in a parasitoid wasp (e.g. Nasonia) and compare the offspring sex ratio with (n-1)/(2n).
